Method of Attack: Provides arbitrary execution of shell commands, arbitrary binary execution, persistence, and update capabilities
Collects system information including architecture and MAC address
Adds registry entry on Windows and creates symbolic links and initrd script on Linux for persistence
Camouflages as MsMpEng.exe process on Windows and as Ubuntu UpdateNotifier utility on Linux
Communicates with C2 server over HTTPS sending BASE64 encoded payload
Receives info, run, execute, and update commands from C2 server allowing operators to run shell commands, execute binaries, and update malware
Attack Vector: Windows version pushed through malvertising with Fallout Exploit Kit
Linux payload dropped via unknown delivery system
Indicators of Compromise: Shared Linux-specific strings like Linux file system paths and kernel thread process names in Windows variant
Symbolic links and initrd script on Linux
Process names MsMpEng.exe (Windows) and Ubuntu UpdateNotifier, [kworker/u8:7-ev] (Linux)
Communication with C2 server over HTTPS with BASE64 encoded payload
